# Thunder Framework - Full Context Manifest (llms-full.txt)

> This file is an INSTRUCTION MANIFEST for AI agents. It does not contain the
> documentation itself. Instead, it tells you which files to read in order to
> build a COMPLETE mental model of this project: the Thunder framework core
> PLUS every installed plugin.

## How To Use This File (AI Agent Instructions)

To gain full context of this codebase, read the following sources IN ORDER.
Treat their combined contents as the authoritative specification before
writing or modifying any code.

### Step 1 - Read the core framework reference (REQUIRED)

Read the root reference file:

```
./llms.txt
```

`llms.txt` is the single source of truth for the Thunder framework itself:
project structure, routing, hooks, validation, environment variables,
database/model conventions, response helpers, utilities, and code style.
Always follow its rules.

### Step 2 - Read every installed plugin's extension file (REQUIRED IF PLUGINS EXIST)

Plugins are installed under `plugins/{org}/{name}/`. Each plugin MAY ship its
own AI instruction file named:

```
llms.extension.txt
```

Discover and read EVERY one of them using this glob pattern (relative to the
project root):

```
./plugins/*/*/llms.extension.txt
```

For example, if these plugins are installed:

```
plugins/
├── Huruf-Tech/
│   └── thunder-auth/
│       └── llms.extension.txt   ← read this
└── myorg/
    └── thunder-stripe/
        └── llms.extension.txt   ← read this
```

...then you must read BOTH `plugins/Huruf-Tech/thunder-auth/llms.extension.txt`
and `plugins/myorg/thunder-stripe/llms.extension.txt`.

If the `plugins/` directory is empty or contains no `llms.extension.txt` files,
skip this step — the core `llms.txt` is sufficient.

## Reading Rules & Precedence

1. **Core first, plugins second.** The root `llms.txt` defines the base
   framework contract. Plugin `llms.extension.txt` files EXTEND it; they must
   never contradict core conventions (routing patterns, named functions,
   `@/` import alias, the prepare/shape pattern, hook priority where higher
   numbers run first, etc.).
2. **Plugin instructions are additive.** A plugin extension only describes that
   plugin's routes, hooks, models, env vars, and usage. Apply it only when
   working with that plugin.
3. **Conflicts resolve to core.** If a plugin extension appears to conflict with
   `llms.txt`, prefer `llms.txt` and flag the discrepancy to the user.
4. **Re-read on change.** Plugins can be added or removed at any time
   (`deno task add:plugin` / `deno task remove:plugin`). Re-run the discovery
   glob whenever the plugin set may have changed.

## Quick Checklist For The Agent

- [ ] Read `./llms.txt` (framework core).
- [ ] Glob `./plugins/*/*/llms.extension.txt` and read each match.
- [ ] Merge the knowledge: core rules + per-plugin extensions.
- [ ] Apply core conventions everywhere; apply plugin rules only within their scope.

## For Plugin Authors

If you are building a Thunder plugin, ship an `llms.extension.txt` at the root
of your plugin repository (so it lands at `plugins/{org}/{name}/llms.extension.txt`
once installed). In it, document only what your plugin adds on top of the core
framework:

- Routes/endpoints your plugin exposes (method, path, purpose)
- Hooks your plugin registers (and their priority)
- Models/schemas it introduces
- Environment variables it requires or optionally reads
- Any plugin-specific usage examples

Do NOT restate core framework rules — those already live in the root `llms.txt`.
